svg.title: A horizontal well drawn as an image
svg.desc: Left: a cross-section of the ground. A vertical typewell gives the reference gamma-ray log, layer by layer. A horizontal well runs sideways through layers that bend and dip; its position in the layers is known up to the PS point and must be predicted after it. Right: the same well drawn as an image. Each column is one step along the well; each row is one foot of depth in the layers, so the layers become flat horizontal bands. The well becomes a line wandering across the bands: dots where it is known, a dashed line where it must be predicted. The reference log runs down the left side and the well's own log along the bottom. Below: the five channels the network reads: the reference log, the well's log, the known positions, a matching cost that is dark where the two logs agree, and the well's dip. Predicting the depth becomes picking one row in every column.
svg.text: The same well, with the layers flattened.
layers dip and bend; the well crosses them
the well's own log, across the columns
What the network reads, stacked like the red, green and blue of a photo.
